parsed.summary: The file formalises the k-colour triangle Ramsey number R_k(3) as the least n such that every k-colouring of the edges of K_n has a monochromatic triangle. It proves four things: R_k(3)^{1/k} → ∞; the explicit lower bound R_k(3) ≥ (c k^{1/3}/log k)^k for all k ≥ 2 with the concrete constant c = 1/(6e^{38}); log R_k(3) is between (1/3−ε) k log k and (1+ε) k log k eventually, for every ε > 0; and log R_k(3) = Θ(k log k). The definitions match the standard notion, and the junk-value conventions only touch finitely many small k, where they are irrelevant. The main caveat is minor: the Lean version fixes a specific constant c, which the excerpt does not state, so it is stronger than the paper as excerpted. The Shannon-capacity corollary is not formalised.

glossary.plain: A k-colouring C of the edges of K_n (on Fin n) such that no colour class contains a triangle (3-clique).
Every k-colouring of E(K_n) contains a monochromatic triangle.
R_k(3) = the least n such that every k-colouring of E(K_n) has a monochromatic triangle.
glossary.note: The set is nonempty for every k by Ramsey's theorem, so sInf is a genuine minimum. For k = 0 the value is 2 (no labeling of K_2 into Fin 0 exists), a degenerate case that does not affect the asymptotic statements.

lean_claims.plain: For every ε > 0, for all sufficiently large k: (1/3−ε) k log k ≤ log R_k(3) ≤ (1+ε) k log k.
log R_k(3) = Θ(k log k) as k → ∞.

paper_claims.plain: There is an absolute constant c > 0 such that R_k(3) ≥ (c k^{1/3}/log k)^k for every integer k ≥ 2.
The Shannon capacity of graphs with independence number 2 is unbounded.

coverage.why: Lean asserts the bound with the explicit constant c = 1/(6e^{38}) rather than merely the existence of some c.
The ε-eventually formulation is exactly the o(1) exponents, taken logarithmically.
log R_k(3) = Θ(k log k) is equivalent to R_k(3) = k^{Θ(k)}.
Shannon capacity is not mentioned in the Lean file.

flags.explanation: Lean fixes c = 1/(6e^{38}), whereas the excerpt only claims that some absolute c exists. This makes Lean stronger; whether this constant is the paper's is not in the excerpt.
The Shannon-capacity reformulation is not formalised.
